subject.title: [Bug]: Gateway heap grows to 1073MB+ at idle on macOS, cron jobs fail silently under memory pressure (ref #86613, #86509)

question: Should the remaining #87109 work stay as one macOS launchd cron stability tracker, or be split between memory-pressure root-cause work and restart-aware failureAlert delivery?
rationale: Source review shows several fixed slices but no single canonical issue or merged fix covers both long-running memory pressure and alert delivery when Gateway itself is wedged.

options.title: Keep open and run a macOS soak
options.body: Use #87109 to drive maintainer-led current-main launchd reproduction, memory-pressure profiling, and failureAlert proof before splitting or closing.

options.title: Split into narrower canonical issues
options.body: Move memory/RSS pressure to the broad Gateway memory tracker and create or link a dedicated restart-aware cron alert tracker.

options.title: Close as covered by partial fixes
options.body: Treat #86701, #86783, and #100867 as sufficient even though the original long-running macOS cron alert scenario remains unproven.

recommendation.title: Keep open and run a macOS soak
recommendation.body: Use #87109 to drive maintainer-led current-main launchd reproduction, memory-pressure profiling, and failureAlert proof before splitting or closing.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved decision is closest to the broad Gateway memory and profiling closure bar rather than the already-fixed watcher or PortGuardian slices.
